overall: Tomorrow (Friday, June 26) in Atlanta is expected to be a partly sunny, warm day with afternoon storm potential. The NWS forecasts a high near 90°F with a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 1pm, driven by southwest flow. No tropical or severe weather context is directly impacting Atlanta; the active Flood Warnings are for the Satilla River in far southeast Georgia (Waycross/Brantley County area), well outside metro Atlanta.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notably wide and warrants caution. ECMWF (89.8°F) and NBM (87.9°F) align closely with the NWS narrative near 90°F, while HRRR comes in cooler at 83.3°F and Weather.com at 84.6°F. The GFS is a significant outlier at just 76.4°F — likely reflecting a persistent cool signal tied to today's observed running max of only 75.2°F — pulling the full ensemble mean down to 82.1°F versus the forecast-only model's 86.7°F.
max_temp_prediction: The most probable temperature range for tomorrow's TMAX is the upper 80s, with the 90-91°F bucket leading the even-set distribution at 23.2% and the odd-set Tier 1 signal pointing to 85-86°F with high confidence (79.9%). The GFS outlier and below-normal today's observed max introduce meaningful downside risk, but the multi-model cluster from ECMWF, NBM, NWS, and Weather.com supports a high in the mid-to-upper 80s. Afternoon convection (40% PoP) could cap the peak slightly if storms arrive before the hottest part of the day.
